title: status.schema.json consumer catalog
content: Load-bearing-contract consumer catalog for plugins/pipeline/schemas/status.schema.json, seeded post-merge of #34 (folds in #42), refreshed post-merge of #53 (merged to main as 055038e, PR #79) because #53 changed the shape of two of the FOUR hand-maintained phase-vocabulary copies this catalog exists to enumerate. PROVENANCE for the #34-era survey, kept as two SHAs deliberately rather than collapsed to one: the three-layer survey was done at d8686bc19d317d89d1ec29b8d2cf13c196bb30ff (the commit the Phase 4 panel actually reviewed); what shipped on main for #34 is 0d0b8d5 (range 1035473..0d0b8d5), released in 0.23.0 as c064b3b. THREE-LAYER SURVEY, re-verified live at #53's merge commit 055038e: (1) application-code call sites: exactly ONE runtime reader in the whole plugin, plugins/pipeline/scripts/voice-lint.mjs -- readFileSync of the schema, key extraction of properties.current_phase.pattern -- and it reads exactly that one key; nothing else in the schema file is consumed at runtime, and #53 did not add a second reader (voice-lint.mjs's run() still decides via `VOICE_MOMENTS[phase] || errorMoment(phase)` and never reads the schema for anything but the shape pattern). (2) data-layer-resident readers: none -- this project has no database function/view bodies; status.json is a flat file artifact, not a stored row. (3) independent re-derivations / other readers: plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md is the GROUND TRUTH writer of current_phase literals (the schema's description field is a hand-maintained mirror of what pipeline.md writes; #42 found it stale once already). halted-error is correctly kept in the schema's pattern despite not being a pipeline.md literal because gate-phase-entry.mjs blesses it by name (cite the symbol, not a line number -- re-derive with `git grep -n 'phase === "halted-error"' -- plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs`). FOUR hand-maintained phase-vocabulary copies exist beyond the schema description and must never be assumed to agree with each other automatically -- THIS IS THE PART #53 CHANGED, and it is why this file was stale between #34 and #53: at #34's merge, voice-lint.mjs's VOICE_MOMENTS/NON_VOICE_PHASES tables were module-PRIVATE (voice-lint.mjs's OWN tables, unreadable from outside), and gate-phase-entry.mjs exported a FOUR-way partition (PREREQUISITES/UNGUARDED/ENTRY/EXIT/TERMINAL -- five names, four semantic cells since ENTRY/EXIT are both derived from PREREQUISITES). As of 055038e: gate-phase-entry.mjs exports a FIFTH partition cell, `PRELUDE = ["0-setup"]` (plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs, re-derive with `git grep -n 'export const PRELUDE'`), consulted by decideForDir in a branch placed AFTER the terminal check (load-bearing ordering: moved earlier, a `0-setup` record carrying `completed_at` would render the setup-step clause instead of the terminal ' is finished.' clause, un-finishing a concluded run); and voice-lint.mjs's VOICE_MOMENTS and NON_VOICE_PHASES are now BOTH EXPORTED (re-derive with `git grep -n 'export const VOICE_MOMENTS\|export const NON_VOICE_PHASES' -- plugins/pipeline/scripts/voice-lint.mjs`) and read by SET MEMBERSHIP from tests/test-voice-lint.sh and tests/test-gate-phase-entry-drift.sh, replacing a substring grep over source text that #53's own root-cause analysis named as unfalsifiable (a phase named only in a comment used to satisfy it). `0-setup` is now declared in NON_VOICE_PHASES (with its mechanism -- Phase 0's one full-voice decision block runs BEFORE the 0-setup write -- and its GENERAL expiry -- wrong the moment any full-voice owner-facing decision block comes to sit between the 0-setup write and the next Checkpoint-first write, tracked at issue #80, filed because that ordering is ALREADY violated at the one owner-facing decision moment in Phase 0's dirty-worktree halt, which #53 explicitly does not fix -- see knowledge/decisions/population-derivation-must-not-narrow-its-own-control.json and the architecture--phase-entry-0setup-prelude-declaration.json entry for the mechanism and expiry in full) and in PRELUDE. The four copies, current as of 055038e: gate-phase-entry.mjs's exported PREREQUISITES/UNGUARDED/TERMINAL/PRELUDE sets (all five names now exported, all readable and set-membership-testable from outside); voice-lint.mjs's now-exported VOICE_MOMENTS/NON_VOICE_PHASES tables; dispatch-model.mjs's KNOWN_PHASES (unchanged by #53 -- already contained the token "0" and phaseKey('0-setup') already resolved to it, token grain not literal grain, so #53 made no change here); and status.schema.json's own current_phase.description example list (unchanged by #53; #53's out_of_scope explicitly refused to touch status.schema.json, 'already names 0-setup correctly'). A FIFTH, TEST-ONLY vocabulary population also exists and is tracked separately (see testing--status-schema-verdict-cap-enforcement.json): Lane 1's two drift derivations (test-voice-lint.sh, test-gate-phase-entry-drift.sh) now claim the SAME 26-literal label SET including 0-setup (widened from 25, replacing five copies of a strict-quoting-form regex with one shared wide pattern per suite plus a bare-word tri-partition form-coverage control), while Lane 2's test-status-schema-contract.sh derives an ASSERTED 27-member set that ADDS halted-error by a stated rule of its own -- the two Lane populations are DIFFERENT BY DESIGN (Lane 2 adds a literal Lane 1 does not write) and #53's own out_of_scope (HANDOFF C) refuses a shared-derivation-helper fix that would collapse that difference, because the helper would have to return the raw EXTRACTION from pipeline.md and never an asserted set, or it would silently delete halted-error from Lane 2. CRITICAL GOVERNANCE FACT carried forward from #34's review, unaffected by #53: nothing in plugins/pipeline/scripts/validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs's AGENT_RULES validates status.json against this schema at all, and that walker does not implement maxLength. So any constraint written into status.schema.json is DOCUMENTATION unless a separate corpus-conformance test enforces it -- see testing--status-schema-verdict-cap-enforcement.json for the enforcement mechanism #34 added. A future change to this schema or to any of the four vocabulary copies must state up front whether it ships a reader or is merely a documented writer-rule, and must re-verify this catalog's three-layer survey rather than assume it still holds -- this file went one issue cycle stale (flagged as a knowledge-drift claim by DBA at #53's Phase 4, resolved here) precisely because 'exported' and 'private' are consumer-shape facts a catalog like this one has to restate on every touching change, not facts that stay true on their own.
